comment: Machine-readable twin of narration-phase1c.md. `tts` is the ElevenLabs synthesis input (FliHub spelled 'Fly Hub'); `caption` keeps the correct spelling. Also used by walkthrough-1c.mjs to pace scene holds (local word-count estimate, no API).

scenes.caption: Sam, the club Owner, opens Athletes and adds Jordan Avery. Next to the public identity — name, gender, nationality — Owners and Admins can record private contact and eligibility details: an email address, a phone number, and notes. They are labeled private, and FliHub enforces that on the server, not just in the interface.
scenes.tts: Sam, the club Owner, opens Athletes and adds Jordan Avery. Next to the public identity — name, gender, nationality — Owners and Admins can record private contact and eligibility details: an email address, a phone number, and notes. They are labeled private, and Fly Hub enforces that on the server, not just in the interface.

scenes.caption: Val is a Viewer in the same organization. She sees Jordan's identity — name, nationality, status — but no email, no phone, no eligibility notes, and no editing controls. Those fields are not hidden in the page; they are never sent to her browser at all.
scenes.tts: Val is a Viewer in the same organization. She sees Jordan's identity — name, nationality, status — but no email, no phone, no eligibility notes, and no editing controls. Those fields are not hidden in the page; they are never sent to her browser at all.

scenes.caption: Back as the Owner: archiving keeps the record and marks it inactive — there is no permanent delete in this phase. Restoring brings the same record back, details intact.
scenes.tts: Back as the Owner: archiving keeps the record and marks it inactive — there is no permanent delete in this phase. Restoring brings the same record back, details intact.

scenes.caption: And for whole rosters, the CSV import adds athletes in bulk — one per row — instead of one form at a time.
scenes.tts: And for whole rosters, the CSV import adds athletes in bulk — one per row — instead of one form at a time.
